name: chart-bar
title: ChartBar
description: Bar chart for single-series magnitude, additive stacked totals, or normalized 0–100% composition across categories.

intent.summary: Bar chart for single-series magnitude, additive stacked totals, or normalized 0–100% composition across categories.
useWhen: Users need to compare one numeric measure across a small set of categories.
Values are grouped into ordered time buckets such as hours, days, weeks, or months and equal visual spacing is appropriate.
A data-viz card needs a compact magnitude comparison rather than a continuous trend.
Several consistent series contribute to each category total or its normalized composition.
avoidWhen: Timestamp positions must reflect irregular elapsed time; pre-bucket the data or use a future continuous time-scale chart.
The visualization needs grouped bars or precise comparison of each individual series across categories.
The interaction requires selection, drill-down, brushing, or zoom.
The data communicates a part-to-whole relationship.

alternatives.when: Users need to follow one or more trends across ordered categories.
alternatives.reason: ChartLine connects ordered observations and supports multiple named series.

alternatives.when: The data communicates parts of a total.
alternatives.reason: ChartDonut provides the part-to-whole composition and center aggregate.

accessibility: Keep category labels concise and provide an adjacent textual summary when exact values are critical to completing a task.
Do not rely on bar color alone to communicate category meaning.
A future interactive tooltip must supplement rather than replace the chart's accessible value representation.
states: The chart is static without hover, selection, loading, or empty-state policy.
Single mode reads data. Stacked and percentage modes read aligned series and categories.
Stacked mode preserves raw totals; percentage mode normalizes every non-empty category to 100%.
An empty dataset renders no bars; the owning card or product supplies meaningful empty-state messaging.
Bars use 2px top corner radii while the lower corners touching the zero axis remain square.
Use one consistent bar color across time buckets when every bar is the same measure at a different interval; categorical color changes are for genuinely distinct categories.
Authored datum colors override the shared categorical palette.
responsiveBehavior: Width and height provide the standalone intrinsic viewport; container constraints are measured and reflow the plot across the available pixels.
Responsive layout changes bar positions and plot extents without scaling SVG text, strokes, corner radii, or margins.
Limit or pre-format long category labels so they remain legible at the chosen width.
Time labels remain ordered, pre-formatted buckets with equal spacing rather than raw continuous timestamps.

customElements: Assign data, series, and categories as JavaScript properties; arrays are not supported as HTML attributes.
react: Pass stable data or series/category arrays; width and height provide standalone intrinsic dimensions while constrained containers reflow automatically.
angular: Bind data or series/categories as properties; width and height provide standalone intrinsic dimensions while constrained containers reflow automatically.

categories.description: X-axis labels for stacked and percentage variants. Set as a JS property.

data.description: Bars to render. Set as a JS property (not an HTML attribute).

height.description: Standalone intrinsic height. Container constraints reflow the plot at rendered pixel size.

series.description: Ordered stack series for stacked and percentage variants. Set as a JS property.

variant.description: Rendering model. Single uses `data`; stacked and percentage use `series` and `categories`.

width.description: Standalone intrinsic width. Container constraints reflow the plot at rendered pixel size.
